title: The 10 Best Engine Stands
subtitle: Rotating engine stands for rebuilds and swaps, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An engine stand holds a pulled engine at working height and lets you roll it over to get at the bottom end. Amazon's best-sellers run from 750 lb stands around $70 to 1,500 lb folding stands near $150, with pro self-locking stands above $400. We ranked 10 on star rating, review volume, and features (1,000 lb or more capacity, a folding frame, locking casters, a tool tray, and self-locking rotation).

avoid.name: EliteEdge Rotating Engine Stand, 3/4 Ton (1,600 lb) Capacity, 4 Casters
avoid.verdict: It claims more capacity than the 1,500 lb stands on our list, on a frame that weighs about the same as a 750 lb stand. The VEVOR 1,300 lb costs about $27 more and publishes a believable rating.
reasons: The title calls 3/4 ton "1,600 lbs". Three-quarters of a ton is 1,500 lb, so even the headline number is wrong.
The listing's shipping weight is 43.3 lb, the same as a seller's 880 lb stand and close to VEVOR's 41 lb, 750 lb model. The 1,500 lb stands here weigh 62 to 77 lb.
It rolls on four casters with no fifth support wheel, the layout the lighter-duty stands use.

buyers_guide.q: How much capacity do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Go by the dressed engine weight, then leave margin. Four-cylinders and most V6s fit on a 750 lb stand. A small-block V8 with heads and intake is often 500 to 600 lb, and big-blocks and diesels run heavier, so a 1,000 to 1,500 lb stand is the safer pick. Stands are often loaded off-center, and that's when the rating matters.

buyers_guide.q: Three casters or four or more?
buyers_guide.a: Three-caster T-base stands are cheap and common, but they tip more easily when you roll a loaded engine over a crack or bump. H-base and U-base stands with four or five casters are steadier. The 1,500 lb VEVOR and the Big Red T26801 both use five.

Only if you're short on space. Folding stands like the VEVOR 1,500 lb (14.8 in. folded), Big Red T26801, and Maxority stand against a wall between projects. Fixed-frame stands are slightly simpler and usually cheaper.

The four adjustable arms fit most domestic and foreign blocks, but check bolt size and length for your engine. Many people buy grade 8 bolts in the right thread so the arms clamp to the block's bellhousing bolt pattern securely.

On a basic stand you pull a pin, rotate, and re-pin; the engine can swing if it's off-balance. A self-locking or geared head, like the Jackco's, holds the engine at any angle, which is safer with a heavy, top-heavy block.
